core.title: Name only existing files and live tool commands in a convention definition's operative prose
core.given: Any convention definition in the repository where the conventions are authored — existing and unchanged, or one you author or edit — whose operative prose (the fields a reader is expected to act on) names a repository path or a tool command
core.when: the convention corpus is validated; also when you write or edit such a definition, or plan to rename or remove a file, or retire a command it quotes
core.then: Every path named in operative prose must exist in the repository and every tool command named must still resolve — a remedy is an executable promise.
prefer: Absent path: correct it to the real location, or drop the pointer if the thing it named no longer exists.
Retired command: replace it with its live replacement.
When retiring a command, record it with its live replacement.
When a plan renames a file or removes a command, include updating every convention definition that quotes it.
avoid: Half-repairs: swapping an absent path for one that is merely plausible — that produced this defect.
A remedy saying only "that command is gone" without the live command — itself unfollowable.
Describing a retired path in present tense — a defect, not a record.
unless: Provenance records (fields recording where a definition was extracted from) — pointing at a deleted file is what provenance is.
Illustrative paths in example or enumeration blocks — fictional by design.
Schematic formula templates — segments are positions, not directories.
A path named as an explicitly excluded mechanism ("no X") — a statement of absence.
A conditional reference ("if it exists", "when present").
Runtime state excluded from version control — checked live, so the exclusion cannot outlive the path.
A path the definition declares retired in past tense — a historical record.
core.why: A remedy is read exactly when the reader is blocked; a missing file or dead command sends them nowhere. Historically nothing read remedies, so a command removal and a check rename left every quoting remedy stale.
evidence: The convention-validation run that checks followability passes.
Each path token in operative prose resolves in the repository, or falls under an authored exception.
Each tool command in operative prose resolves; retired commands appear only with their live replacement or in past-tense records.
verification: Strict disposition: the check fails on every finding — no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline; severity 3. The disposition is the point: strict is chosen because the authored exceptions absorb the historical bulk of apparent findings, leaving a small, affordable residue.

Scope of scan: every convention definition in the authoring repository — existing and unchanged ones included, not only those a current plan touches. The corpus location and file identification come from the profile.

Prose scope: the check reads only operative prose — the fields a reader is expected to act on. Provenance (a record) and examples (illustrations) are excluded: only operative prose makes a promise. The exact field split comes from the profile.

Finding: operative prose naming a repository path that does not exist, or a tool command that no longer resolves against the stack's live command surface. A retired command is a finding unless it appears with its live replacement or in a past-tense record.

The exception classification is owned by the checker: distinguishing provenance, illustration, schematic templates, excluded mechanisms, conditional references, past-tense retired records, and version-control-ignored state — the ignore check is re-run live so the exclusion cannot outlive the path.

The check runs only where the conventions are authored (the source repository of the convention corpus); it does not cover repositories that merely consume the conventions from an installed package, where quoted paths cannot resolve.

values: operative prose added or edited naming a repository path or a tool command

fires: A validation run finds an existing, unchanged convention definition whose remedy names a file that does not exist — even if the current plan never touched that definition.
A convention definition's operative prose still instructs a tool command that has been removed from the toolchain.
An author writes or edits a remedy naming a path that does not exist in the repository.
A plan renames a file or removes a tool command while convention definitions still quote the old spelling.
doesNotFire: The path appears only in a provenance record.
The path appears in an example or enumeration block as an illustration.
The path is a segment position in a schematic formula, an explicitly excluded mechanism, a conditional reference, version-control-ignored runtime state, or is described in past tense as retired.
The run is in a repository that consumes the conventions from an installed package rather than the repository where they are authored (the check is gated to the authoring repository).

profileRequirements.meaning: How a convention definition's fields divide into operative prose (strings a reader is expected to act on) versus provenance records and illustrative example blocks — only operative prose makes a promise.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Operative: `fix_hint`, `operational_guidance`, `normative_text`, `statement`, term `text`, `notes`, `description`. Excluded: provenance (`source.legacy_path` + `legacy_sha`) and `examples`/`values` blocks.

profileRequirements.meaning: How the convention schema represents schematic path templates — path-like strings whose segments are positions, not directories — so the followability check can recognize and exclude them.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Schematic `Formula:` templates — e.g. `Formula: ... -> contracts/theme/seg1/...` — segments are positions, not directories.

neutralityNotes: The subject was generalized from ATDD's 'convention node' to 'convention definition', from 'CLI verb' to 'tool command', from 'checkout' to 'repository', and from 'fix_hint' to 'remedy'. Everything the core needs from the stack is expressed with closed-vocabulary keys: the corpus location (roots.conventions), the file-kind identification (suffix.convention_node), the operative/provenance/illustration field split and the schematic-template marker (idiom.convention_graph#convention_operative_fields, idiom.convention_graph#schematic_templates). The scan-all-nodes obligation and the authoring-repository gate are rule-level obligations and stay in core:verification. The retired-verb mapping, validator and test ids, the platform-gate function, the VCS ignore command and the calibration counts have no stack-neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly. Per-rule severity 3 and the strict disposition stay with the rule in core:verification, not the profile. If a stack authors no convention corpus of its own, this rule is vacuous there.
